title: Make it feel like yours.
route: Keep the working product. Test one visual choice before redesigning anything else.
approvalScope: No experiments authorised. Say begin in your agent conversation when you are ready.
goal: A small, useful app you enjoy opening and feel proud to share.
obstacle: The latest polish pass looks competent, but the result does not feel like the product you wanted.
preserved: The ability to compare against the current version
assumptions: This is an illustrative scenario, not an inspection of your project.
The dissatisfaction can be narrowed to a visible choice; the first experiment tests that assumption.
alternatives: Keep the existing design and replace only the visual treatment.
Reduce the product to the one screen that preserves its original appeal.

tasks.title: Find the visual mismatch
tasks.try: Inspect one representative screen beside the experience you wanted.
tasks.learn: Which visible choice is making the whole product feel wrong?
tasks.unlock: A precise question for a small design comparison.

image.alt: A screen with one region isolated for closer inspection.
image.label: Concept / isolate the question

details.label: Deliverable
details.text: One annotated screenshot, with a single comparison question.

details.label: Evidence to collect
details.text: The current screen, the intended reference, and the user's reaction to the marked difference.

details.label: Stop when
details.text: One visual question is specific enough to build alternatives for. Do not start polishing.

details.label: Undo
details.text: Only an annotation is created. Product files stay untouched.

outcomes.label: If supported
outcomes.text: Use the isolated question to scope U2.

outcomes.label: If refuted
outcomes.text: Check whether the disappointing part is the workflow rather than its appearance.

outcomes.label: If inconclusive
outcomes.text: Request a reaction to the annotated screen before proposing another experiment.

tasks.title: Compare one design choice
tasks.try: Build a small comparison on the same screen, content and behaviour.
tasks.learn: Which direction actually feels better when you can see it?
tasks.unlock: A chosen direction, grounded in your reaction.

image.alt: Two equally sized screen treatments using the same content.
image.label: Concept / compare fairly

details.label: Deliverable
details.text: A rendered comparison with equally finished candidates.

details.label: Evidence to collect
details.text: Your pick and what made it appealing. The agent does not choose for you.

details.label: Stop when
details.text: The candidates can answer U1's question. Wait for your judgment before U3.

details.label: Undo
details.text: Keep the candidates in an isolated prototype; the current product remains the control.

outcomes.label: If supported
outcomes.text: Take your chosen direction into U3.

outcomes.label: If refuted
outcomes.text: Record what all candidates missed and revise the question.

outcomes.label: If inconclusive
outcomes.text: Identify the difference the comparison failed to isolate.

tasks.title: Try it on a second screen
tasks.try: Apply the chosen direction to a different representative screen.
tasks.learn: Does the improvement hold beyond the first carefully chosen example?
tasks.unlock: Evidence for a focused change, or a clear reason to change course.

image.alt: A selected visual treatment connected to a second screen.
image.label: Concept / test the reach

details.label: Deliverable
details.text: A second-screen prototype beside the first candidate.

details.label: Evidence to collect
details.text: The user's judgment on the new screen and checks of its existing behaviour.

details.label: Stop when
details.text: The direction has been tested on the second screen. Broader rollout is a separate proposal.

details.label: Undo
details.text: Discard the isolated prototype without removing the comparison evidence.

outcomes.label: If supported
outcomes.text: Propose a focused implementation batch for approval.

outcomes.label: If refuted
outcomes.text: Keep the first-screen finding and narrow where this direction applies.

outcomes.label: If inconclusive
outcomes.text: Name the missing observation; avoid a broad redesign on weak evidence.
